svg.text: PEDAL ADAPTATION 1 — Blackface Preamp / Drive (9 V, JFET + op-amp)
The tube circuit re-expressed at pedal voltages: JFET stands in for V1A, the stack is the SAME passive network, an op-amp replaces V1B, diodes replace power-tube saturation.
Trim Rs (2k trimmer) so drain sits ≈ 5–6 V. 2N5457/J201/MPF102 all work.
② Passive TMB stack (same network as the amp)
Insertion loss ≈ -17 dB at the mids with all knobs at 10; deeper scoop as MID is lowered.
Same values as the amp. Use 250k pots (B for treble, A for bass), 10k linear for mid.
③ Volume (+bright) and U1A recovery gain
Gain = 1 + Rf/Rg ≈ 22 (27 dB). Replaces V1B; makes up the ≈ -17 dB stack loss.
TL072 / TL082 / NE5532, single +9V supply, Vref = ½ supply.
Gain = 1 + DRIVE/4.7k (0 → 22× with the pot fully up; keep a 1k stopper in series so it never reaches 0 Ω).
Output level ≈ ±0.6 V on one polarity and ±1.2 V on the other = the asymmetric 'push-pull gets lopsided' character.
Diodes across the feedback resistor soft-clip the stage like a pushed power section.
CAB-SIM ≈ 2-pole low-pass (-3 dB ≈ 3 kHz): use it going straight to a mixer/interface,
bypass it when feeding a real power amp and speaker cabinet.
Build tip: 9 V gives ≈ ±3 V of headroom. For cleaner Twin-style
headroom run the op-amps from 18 V (TL072 rated) and double the Vref

Reverb and tremolo are deliberately left out of the pedal (spring tank + 12AT7 driver are bulky); use a dedicated reverb/tremolo pedal after it. Circuit values are a starting point: socket the JFET and trim by ear.
